2026-09-08.title: Your Computer Is Basically a Very Fast Idiot
2026-09-08.subtitle: It renders movies, runs games, and holds video calls — by doing one mind-numbingly simple thing a few billion times a second.

tg_quiz.correct: Yep — one dumb loop, billions of times a second.
tg_quiz.wrong: Nope — it just loops: fetch, decode, execute.
tg_quiz.explain: Everything 'smart' is that tiny loop stacked into a tower.

2026-09-08.title: Money Is a Story We All Agree to Believe
2026-09-08.subtitle: The cash in your pocket is worthless paper. The number in your bank isn't even paper. So why does the whole world chase it?

tg_quiz.q: What actually backs a modern banknote?
options: Shared trust that others will accept it
tg_quiz.correct: Exactly — money is a story we all agree to believe.
tg_quiz.wrong: Not gold — it's collective trust, backed by law.
tg_quiz.explain: Value lives in the network of people who accept it, not the paper.

2026-09-08.title: Stop Thinking in Yes/No. Start Thinking in Odds.
2026-09-08.subtitle: Almost nothing is certain, yet your brain demands a yes or a no. Learning to answer in numbers is the single biggest upgrade to how you think.

tg_quiz.q: Flip a fair coin twice — chance of heads both times?
tg_quiz.correct: Nice — AND means multiply: ½ × ½ = ¼.
tg_quiz.wrong: Close — for 'both', multiply: ½ × ½ = ¼.
